speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; could you tell me your age and when your high blood pressure was first noticed? Also, have you experienced any headaches, shortness of breath, or changes in urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given his age and the unexpected finding of hypertension, are you noticing any headaches, visual changes, or abdominal pain at home? Also, has he had any recent infections, or do you notice any swelling in his legs or face?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: That is a very specific finding; has the blood pressure been measured in his other arm, both legs, and are you noticing any differences in the strength of the pulses in his extremities? I would also like to listen to his heart and neck for any unusual sounds, so may I perform a cardiovascular examination now?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Blood Pressure in all four extremities. REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: ECG. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest X-Ray. REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram.

Have you felt a delay between the radial pulse in his arm and the femoral pulse in his leg, or noticed any weak pulses in his lower extremities? I also need to know if he has ever had episodes of cold hands or feet, or if he gets winded easily during play.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure in Upper Extremities: 150/80 mm Hg (Right) with noted lower values in lower extremities. Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses. Echocardiogram: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation; left ventricular function is normal. Heart Auscultation: Normal S1 and S2, 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back. Chest X-ray: Normal heart size, no rib notching observed. Renal Ultrasound and ECG results are not available in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of high blood pressure in the arms, weak leg pulses, and the echocardiogram showing aortic narrowing confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.
